source_snapshot.procedure: Assert TPM physical presence; enable Secure Boot/TPM; change Security Boot to `another mode`; save/reboot; verify changed.
source_snapshot.criteria: Security mode can be changed successfully.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: CRITICAL; requires exact trust-state matrix, key implications and recovery.

old_problem: `Another mode` leaves source, target and final Secure Boot/TPM/key states undefined. Physical-presence jumper identity/power procedure, encryption/key consequences, dual-plane oracle and rollback are absent.
disposition_reason: ED-11 prohibits arbitrary/all/random BIOS setting changes. Secure Boot modes, key databases and TPM ownership are not interchangeable runtime identifiers; choosing them can invalidate boot signatures or sealed secrets. The core security transition and recovery must be owner-approved.
decision_basis: Direct XLSX rows 2258 and 2259, same-row AI fields, GPT V2, historical record and unique identity were reviewed.
Preserve TPM physical presence, F1 Security page, Secure Boot/TPM enable, mode change, save/reboot and changed-state evidence.
Require exact initial→target→final matrix including Secure Boot enable/mode, PK/KEK/db/dbx state and TPM enable/ownership.
A qualified operator identifies and manipulates the board control under approved power/ESD procedure; automation only collects read-only evidence.
Require recovery keys/media, configuration backup, firmware+OS corroboration, boot/encryption health and final restoration.
No jumper/switch action, BIOS change, key/TPM operation, reboot, log clear or DUT action occurred.

test_case.test_name: Operator-controlled Secure Boot/TPM mode transition and restoration
test_case.purpose: Prove one explicitly named Secure Boot/TPM trust-state transition survives reboot and remains observable and bootable, then restore the approved final state and physical control.
required_package: SUT/board/BIOS/TPM build and supported state matrix
Signed initial/target/final Secure Boot, key and TPM ownership states
Recovery keys/media, backup, console and boot/encryption oracle
test_case.test_command: Gate closed. A qualified operator records baseline, asserts the exact physical-presence control, applies only the named BIOS security transition, saves/reboots once and restores the control; collect firmware and OS Secure Boot/TPM/key/boot evidence, then perform and verify the signed final-state restoration.
test_case.expected_result: Every approved target security/key/TPM state is active after reboot, firmware and OS evidence agree, boot/encryption health remains normal, and final BIOS/key/TPM plus physical-control state equals the signed restoration matrix.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires a named state matrix, exact physical procedure, dual-plane evidence and verified recovery/final state. `Changed` alone cannot pass. Undefined `another mode`, missing keys or rollback keeps Pending; boot/encryption failure is FAIL.
safety_gate: Dedicated recoverable SUT and protected recovery material.
Qualified operator and exact board-control/power/ESD procedure.
One approved reversible transition; no arbitrary mode/key/TPM reset.
Stop on boot, encryption, TPM, key or logging anomaly; no retry.
expected_evidence: Physical control mapping and operator evidence
OS Secure Boot/TPM corroboration and reboot timeline
test_case.recovery: On boot/security failure, do not toggle other modes or clear TPM/keys. Preserve console/firmware evidence and use only the signed recovery media, keys and BIOS restoration path.

source_conflict.reason: `Another mode` remains an undefined core security target, so the source cannot yet yield deterministic success.
